In earthworm, ammonia is converted into urea in chloragogen cell which is released into either coelomic fluid or blood. 8.3.6 NERVOUS SYSTEM IN EARTHWORM Nervous system is responsible for regulating and coordinating various activities of the body in proper way. It has main role in responding stimuli, maintaining internal environment of the body and coordinating various functions of the body. Nervous system in Pheretima is well developed and concentrated type. It is divisible into central nervous system, peripheral nervous system and sympathetic nervous system Biology, Grade 11 | 370

Figure 8.3.16 Nervous system of earthworm 1. Central nervous system (CNS) Central nervous system is formed by an anteriorly situated nerve ring and a rod like ventral nerve cord arising posteriorly from it. a. Nerve ring: Nerve ring is situated around the pharynx in 3rd and 4th segment. It is formed by a pair of fused supra pharyngeal ganglia, a pair of circum pharyngeal connective and a pair of fused subpharyngeal ganglia. Supra-pharyngeal or cerebral ganglia are also called brain which are white coloured and pear-shaped structures lying dorsally in the groove between the buccal cavity and the pharynx. From the either side of cerebral ganglia arises laterally a thick and Figure 8.3.17 Nervous system of earthworm in lateral view strong circum or peripharyngeal connective. These connectives encircle pharynx and meet at the ventral side with sub-pharyngeal ganglia in 4th segment. b. Ventral nerve cord: Ventral nerve cord is a long rod like structure arising from sub-pharyngeal ganglia. It runs posteriorly along the mid-ventral line up to the last segment of the body. While passing, it gets slightly enlarged or swelled in each segment forming segmental ganglion. Ventral nerve cord Biology, Grade 11 | 371

is actually double, though it appears single externally. Hence, it is formed by the fusion of two longitudinal rod like structures; right longitudinal cord and left longitudinal cord. It means a segmental ganglion is also formed by the fusion of a pair of ganglia, one belonging to each cord of double ventral nerve cord. Histologically, ventral nerve cord is composed of nerve cells and nerve fibres. The ventral nerve cord is enclosed in a sheath composed of three layers-Outer visceral peritoneum, middle layer of longitudinal muscle fibres and inner thick fibrous layer of epineurium Figure 8.3.18 T.S of ventral nerve cord 2. Peripheral nervous system The peripheral nervous system is formed by the several nerves which arise from central nervous system. From each cerebral ganglion arise about 8 to 10 nerves innervating the prostomium and buccal chamber. Two pairs of nerves arising from circum-pharyngeal connectives supply the first segment and buccal cavity. Similarly, three pairs of nerves from sub- pharyngeal ganglia supply the various structures present in 2nd, 3rd and 4th segment. From each segmental ganglia arises laterally three pairs of nerves called segmental nerves; one pair anteriorly and next two pairs posteriorly. Segmental nerves innervate the wall of alimentary canal, body wall and other visceral organs of respective segments. All the nerves are of mixed type functioning as both afferent and efferent nerves. 3. Sympathetic nervous system Sympathetic nervous system consists of an extensive nerve network or plexus spreading beneath the epidermis and within the muscles of body wall, on the wall of alimentary canal and other visceral organs. These plexuses are finally connected with the circum pharyngeal connectives.

Activity 8.9 Visit the laboratory with your biology teacher and dissect the freshly preserved earthworm to identify its nerve ring, ventral nerve cord and nerves. Draw a labelled diagram of it on the chart paper. Present in the class for discussion.

SENSE ORGANS IN EARTHWORM Sense organs are simple and well developed in earthworm which consists of single cell or group of ectodermal cells. They are of following types: i. Epidermal receptors: They are scattered throughout the epidermis layer of body wall and more abundant in lateral side and ventral surface.
